dos_donts.tip: Greet warmly with a smile and eye contact
A handshake is common: firm for men, light for women
Dress modestly when visiting churches or monasteries, with shoulders and knees covered
Use both hands or the right hand when giving or receiving items
Do not refuse tea bluntly; tea (shai) is a big part of the culture
Avoid discussing politics, especially Russia, or religion
Do not touch someone's head
Do not point your feet at people or sacred objects
Vegetarians should specify no meat (bez myasa) as samsa, plov and lagman often contain minced meat
Soups that look vegetarian, such as lentil or noodle, may be meat-based unless you ask
Use a translation app or written Russian phrases to overcome the language barrier
Offer a handshake when greeting someone in formal situations

scams.tip: Unofficial taxis may charge 2-3 times the local rate; use Yandex Go or negotiate clearly before entering
Helpful strangers at ATMs may try to steal card details or money; use ATMs inside banks or malls and cover your PIN
Unofficial exchange stalls may offer fake or rigged rates
Petition or survey scam: someone asks you to sign a petition then demands a donation; politely decline and walk away
Fake police officers are rare but possible; ask for ID, as real officers won't ask for money, and call the emergency number or walk to a public space
Beware of aggressive street vendors or unsolicited guides in touristy areas
Unofficial taxis may charge 2-3x the local rate; use Yandex Go or negotiate clearly before entering
Unofficial exchange stalls may offer fake or rigged rates; exchange money only at banks or licensed exchange counters
Fake police officers are rare but possible and may demand a bribe; ask for ID, as real officers won't ask for money, and call the emergency number or walk to a public space
